requirements.text: One small closable PETG enclosure accepts interchangeable separately printed TPU liners and a loose metal nut.

provenance.statement: User requests one small PETG exterior, closable, with TPU inserts and space to shake a stock metal nut.

questions.criterion: Full pair clears the established shell and pad insertion path; 0.2 mm squeeze is explicit.

requirements.text: The floor, ceiling and all four interior walls have TPU damping coverage.

provenance.statement: User explicitly requires damping on the bottom, top, and all four walls.

questions.criterion: Continuous skins cover floor, pad and four walls.

requirements.text: All object-contact interior faces are flat; damping structures are inside the liner.

provenance.statement: User clarification: the interior needs to be flat for the objects, while the liner may have structures inside.

questions.criterion: The complete contents cavity has planar contact faces without marking protrusions.

requirements.text: Several permanently labeled CAD-defined internal damping configurations can be printed together.

provenance.statement: User asks for labeled variants, explicit CAD structures rather than infill, and a batch print; additional variants are welcome.

questions.criterion: Separated B-style ties and posts retain open core spaces.

requirements.text: Use research to inform a reusable damping experiment and compare variants by shaking the same metal nut.

provenance.statement: User requests research on effective damping structures and plans to report which liner performs best.

questions.criterion: Compare T08/T16 physically with cavity-size difference explicit.

requirements.text: Prioritize maximum quietness in a thin liner and recommend a focused print batch with a solid control and the most promising candidates.

provenance.statement: User follow-up: maximize quietness while keeping it thin; provide a STEP set focused on more confident candidates and retain control A.

questions.criterion: Compare damping against approved B/S with the same nut and shell.

requirements.text: Thinner follow-up liners retain both continuous inner and outer TPU skins for stable printing.

provenance.statement: User reports I10 shell-side print damage, says both walls are needed, and requests one or two significantly thinner stable variants; slicer changes are allowed.

requirements.text: Provide roughly 30 mm square flat plate samples, four to eight designs printable together, with filled exterior edges.

provenance.statement: User requests four to eight roughly three-centimetre square bottom-plate samples rather than full boxes, filled exterior overhangs and a flat test face.

requirements.text: Explore structures that reduce visible surface lines and waviness beyond the current 50% ironing result.

provenance.statement: User reports visible surface waviness despite improvement at 50% ironing and requests several internal structure experiments.

questions.criterion: Compare object-facing finish and seam/string artifacts physically.

requirements.text: Keep damping usefulness as a later physical test; S16 remains the preferred baseline.

provenance.statement: User names S16 as the best so far and says damping must still be tested later while initially focusing on surface texture.

questions.criterion: Thicker upright skins retain useful damping.

requirements.text: All four support-test variants must use Classic, without Arachne.

provenance.statement: During implementation the user explicitly reiterates: I do not want Arachne.

questions.criterion: Actual supplied TPU process uses Classic at ordinary widths without thin-wall recovery.

requirements.text: Provide four labeled complete cup/lid-insert pairs for the existing experiment box: A at 1.6 and 2.0 mm; B at 1.6 mm with two distinct tie sizes.

provenance.statement: User accepts both SVG explanations and requests four printable variants, matching lids and markings: A at 16/20 and B at 16 with two distinct tie sizes; the S16 context establishes 1.6/2.0 mm units.

requirements.text: The replacements must retain wall paths with the ordinary repository default slicing process.

provenance.statement: Asked which slicer/nozzle/line width/profile was used for the failure, the user answers: default as in the repo. They allow increased A thickness if needed, prioritising reliable Classic slicing.

requirements.text: The four replacements must generate their wall skins with ordinary Classic slicing, without Arachne or dependence on thin-wall recovery.

provenance.statement: User reports wall paths missing on all four variants, declines printing the batch, and requests investigation and repair for normal slicing without Arachne.

requirements.text: Find a thin liner that survives installation and handling with mutually supported walls and bottom.

provenance.statement: User reports further dental-liner breakage during insertion and requests support experiments to find the minimum usable thickness without breakage.

questions.criterion: Insert and handle without tears or detached ties.

requirements.text: Provide two labeled solid cup/lid-pad controls, C12 at 1.2 mm and C16 at 1.6 mm, for the existing experiment shell, without internal structures.

provenance.statement: User reports all four new pairs printed but untested. After touching B16 they request two solid variants, optionally named C, at spoken 12/16; the prior S16/A16 context establishes 1.2/1.6 mm units. No interior design is wanted.

requirements.text: Provide T08/T16 complete cup/pad pairs for the existing test shell, with compact M1 markings.

provenance.statement: After choosing T08 and T16 as the next prints and reviewing marking SVGs, user asks to create the boxes with M1 to prepare for printing.

questions.criterion: The delivered pair has current matching source/STEP/STL and reviewed wall, gap and label paths.
Print and install the full cup/pad without breakage; verify fit and readability.

requirements.text: Minimize marking footprint while keeping IDs visible and protecting the structure being tested.

provenance.statement: User reports existing bottom text too big/deep and asks to preserve the functional skin; later selects M1 compact corner text.

questions.criterion: Matching M1 IDs are recessed one layer and fully backed by local solid corners, outside the central floor.
Both compact IDs are visible on printed black TPU.

requirements.text: Keep corners solid for a reasonable distance to reduce corner print defects.

provenance.statement: User requests solid corner regions to avoid defects near corners; no numerical distance is specified.

questions.criterion: All wall channels stop 4 mm before tangent ends; floor and pad corners are solid.
Solid corners print cleanly in the full cup.

decisions.text: Retain 34 mm cup, B 1.6 mm horizontal sandwiches/.8 mm posts and .2 mm squeeze. Change upright skins to .8/1.6 around .6 gap; solid 4 mm wall-end lands and 10 x 6.5 mm floor/pad label corner seats. M1 strokes .8, .2 recess, widened .6 inter-glyph spacing within the accepted reserved footprint.

hypotheses.text: Thicker skins may reduce joint marks; actual damping, finish, strength and readability remain physical.
